local_cases.name: León, Spain — total solar eclipse
local_cases.source_notes: NASA lists local contact times rounded to the minute. Converted from Europe/Madrid summer time (CEST, UTC+02:00). Observer coordinates are the project's catalogue point for León; NASA's city table does not publish the exact observing coordinates.

local_cases.name: Dallas, Texas — total solar eclipse
local_cases.source_notes: NASA local circumstances are rounded to the minute and shown in CDT (UTC-05:00), converted here to UTC. Coordinates are approximate Dallas city-centre coordinates, not a station-level coordinate published by NASA.

local_cases.name: Albuquerque, New Mexico — annular solar eclipse
local_cases.source_notes: NASA local circumstances are rounded to the minute and shown in MDT (UTC-06:00), converted here to UTC. Coordinates are approximate Albuquerque city-centre coordinates, not a station-level coordinate published by NASA.

local_cases.name: London, United Kingdom — partial solar eclipse
local_cases.source_notes: The published local timetable lists London first contact 10:09, maximum 10:59 and end 11:51 BST. Times are converted to UTC (BST=UTC+01:00 on 2022-10-25). Coordinates are approximate London city-centre coordinates, not a survey station. NASA's GSFC Solar Eclipse Search Engine independently identifies 2022-10-25 as a partial eclipse and gives greatest eclipse at 11:00:07 UT; see https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEsearch/SEdata.php?Ecl=+20221025.

global_maximum_cases.name: 2026-08-12 — geocentric greatest eclipse
global_maximum_cases.source_notes: NASA's 2026 eclipse catalogue rounds greatest eclipse to 17:46 UT and lists ΔT=75.4 s. The comparison uses a 30-second tolerance because the published time is rounded to the minute; the project calculates with DE440s/Skyfield.

global_maximum_cases.name: 2023-04-20 — hybrid solar eclipse, geocentric greatest eclipse
global_maximum_cases.source_notes: NASA GSFC identifies this as a hybrid solar eclipse and publishes the instant of greatest eclipse as 04:16:44.8 UT. This regression checks the geocentric greatest-eclipse epoch only; the expected_eclipse_type field records the source's event classification and is not a computed classification at every location. NASA's published Besselian realization uses VSOP87/ELP2000-85 and Delta-T=70.3 s; EclipseKit's configured DE440s realization may differ slightly, so the 30-second tolerance is a screening threshold, not a universal accuracy claim.
